item.title: Steiner Digs In at Ocado as Warehouse Tech Unit Falters
item.description: Ocado Group Plc Chief Executive Officer Tim Steiner said he remains committed to leading the British grocery delivery company, as it announced another weak performance from its key technology division.

item.title: DCC Gets Sweetened Bid From KKR, ECP After Drawn-Out Talks
item.description: KKR & Co. and Energy Capital Partners have sweetened their bid for DCC Plc to more than £5.7 billion ($7.7 billion) and bought extra time to complete what’s become a drawn-out takeover process.

item.title: HSBC Upgrades Indian Stocks as Earnings Risk from Oil Subsides
item.description: HSBC Holdings Plc. raised Indian equities to neutral citing receding risks to earnings from oil prices and strong domestic consumption, reflecting strengthening confidence in the nation’s stock market.

item.title: Market Is So Risk-On That Path Higher Looks Tough: Taking Stock
item.description: Bullish equity investors have embraced a Goldilocks scenario, driving risk-on sentiment to the point where it’s harder to identify what will trigger the next leg higher.

item.title: Japan’s Household Inflation Expectations Hit Highest Since 2006
item.description: Inflation expectations among Japan’s households climbed to the highest level in data back to 2006, supporting Bank of Japan’s stance to keep raising interest rates.

item.title: Uber Agrees to Buy Delivery Hero in $14.8 Billion Deal
item.description: Uber Technologies Inc. has agreed to buy Delivery Hero SE in a deal that values the German food-delivery company at $14.8 billion.

item.title: UK Economy Grows as Services Defy Energy, Political Turmoil
item.description: The UK economy unexpectedly grew in May, suggesting that consumers and businesses were more resilient than feared in the face of political turbulence and the Iran war energy shock.

item.title: EQT Raises Offer Price for Kakaku.com Above Bid by LY, Bain
item.description: EQT AB is increasing its tender offer price for Japan’s Kakaku.com Inc., escalating its bidding war with the duo of LY Corp. and Bain Capital for the online data firm.

item.title: TSMC to Spend $265 Billion on US Buildout in Key Trump Deal
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. plans to spend an additional $100 billion to expand US chipmaking capacity, formalizing a pledge that’s part of a larger deal between Washington and Taipei to bring semiconductor manufacturing to American soil.

item.title: Lagarde Watchers Cast Aside Doubts to Say She’ll Finish ECB Term
item.description: Christine Lagarde keeps stoking speculation that her presidency of the European Central Bank may soon end, but most economists reckon she’ll serve out her term.

item.title: FTSE 100 Live: UK Economy Grew Unexpectedly in May
item.description: FTSE 100 Live: UK Economy Grew Unexpectedly in May【原文：FTSE 100 Live: UK Economy Grew Unexpectedly in May】

item.title: S. Africa Finance Chief Reviews $219 Billion Fund CEO Suspension
item.description: South Africa’s finance minister said the board of the continent’s biggest money manager briefed the government on a decision to suspend its chief executive officer over alleged governance issues and that it will assess the information after talks with those involved.

item.title: TSMC Hikes Sales, Spending Outlook to Signal AI ‘Megatrend’
item.description: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. raised its spending and revenue projections for the year, reflecting its confidence that torrid growth in demand for chips and data centers will extend into 2027.

item.title: Citigroup’s Indian Clients Shift Focus to Rupee Volatility
item.description: Citigroup Inc. says its Indian corporate clients are expecting the rupee will keep weakening and are looking for products that will enable them to profit from its volatility.

item.title: IEA Sees $6.5 Trillion At Risk if China Imposes Rare-Earth Curbs
item.description: China’s rare earth export curbs could put $6.5 trillion of downstream production outside the country at risk each year if fully implemented, the International Energy Agency warned in a report on rare earths and critical minerals.

item.title: Nickel Hits Three-Week High on Indonesia Supply Risks, Fed View
item.description: Nickel climbed to a three-week high as expectations for Federal Reserve rate hikes faded, while uncertainty over mining policy in top producer Indonesia clouded the supply outlook.

item.title: China Internet Stocks Catch an AI Lift as Beijing Warms to Tech
item.description: China’s internet stocks are mounting a comeback after a prolonged period of lagging the broader market, buoyed by improving earnings expectations, signs of policy support and optimism around the country’s artificial intelligence progress.

item.title: Fidelity Plans to Rebuild Gold Holdings on Long-Term Bull Case
item.description: Asset manager Fidelity International Ltd. plans at some point to add back gold positions that it cut earlier this year, confident that bullion’s long-term drivers remain intact.

item.title: Syngenta’s $5 Billion Hong Kong IPO Is Said to Face Fresh Delays
item.description: Syngenta Group’s planned $5 billion Hong Kong initial public offering is facing delays as the seed and pesticide company waits for better conditions in the agriculture sector, according to people familiar with the matter.

item.title: Asian Gas Prices Rise to Highest Since March on Mideast Tensions
item.description: Asian liquefied natural gas prices rose to the highest since late March as fresh hostilities in the Middle East deepened concerns that shipping through the key Strait of Hormuz will remain disrupted for longer.

item.title: Japan’s Katayama Leaves Open Possibility of GPIF Domestic Shift
item.description: Japanese Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama reiterated that she will pursue measures to encourage the Government Pension Investment Fund to invest more in domestic financial assets, while stressing she has no authority to step into the fund’s investment decisions.

item.title: Japan’s Robot Makers Join Nvidia’s Physical AI Cosmos Coalition
item.description: Nvidia Corp. and four of Japan’s leading industrial automation companies said they will expand their collaboration on robot development, bolstering Jensen Huang’s push into AI-enabled hardware.

item.title: China Seeks to Curb New Bond Sales by LGFVs With Increased Debt
item.description: A major Chinese bond regulator is taking fresh steps to curb debt sales by the nation’s municipal borrowers, according to people familiar with the matter, adding pressure on weaker issuers looking to refinance notes.

item.title: Nvidia’s Huang Courts Japanese Suppliers With Kanda Pork Skewers
item.description: On Wednesday night, Jensen Huang was in Tokyo’s central Kanda district courting the little-known Japanese suppliers that underpin the AI supply chain.

item.title: Wheat Holds Near Two-Month High After Black Sea Attacks
item.description: Wheat futures held gains after jumping 5% on Wednesday, as Ukrainian and Russian strikes in the Black Sea threatened a key export route for the warring countries.

item.title: Greer Praises Swiss Investments as US Weighs Tariff Decision
item.description: Trade Representative Jamieson Greer offered praise for Switzerland’s stance in trade negotiations and its investments in the US, a positive sign for the European nation as it looks to secure a 15% tariff and avoid further confrontation with President Donald Trump.

item.title: Hyundai to Buy SoftBank’s Boston Dynamics Stake in Robot Push
item.description: Hyundai Motor Co. and its affiliates are moving to acquire SoftBank Group Corp.’s remaining stake in the automaker’s Boston Dynamics unit, as the Seoul-based company accelerates commercialization of its Atlas humanoid robot.

item.title: Adani Flagship Draws Mutual Fund Interest as Governance Risks Recede
item.description: Local mutual funds bought Adani Enterprises shares worth 46.60 billion rupees last month.

item.title: Palm Beach Strikes Down Data Center Plan After Local Backlash
item.description: Palm Beach County commissioners rejected a proposal late Wednesday to build a digital infrastructure hub to house AI data centers and warehouses, voting in line with the ardent opposition from local residents.

item.title: Pound Index Hits One-Year High on Mahmood for Chancellor Reports
item.description: A measure of sterling’s strength rose to its highest level in a year on Wednesday following reports that incoming UK Prime Minister Andy Burnham will name Shabana Mahmood as his Chancellor of the Exchequer.
